vectors.note: Chain 002 run with its true head, so the EX-15 check passes.

End-truncation is NOT detectable from the export alone — a prefix of a valid chain is a valid chain. VALID is the correct verdict here, not a verifier bug; the paired vector that supplies --head over these same bytes is what catches it.
Legal extremes: 1-char and 200-char titles, choice_count 2 and 64, choice 0 and choice_count-1.
A non-ASCII title stored as literal UTF-8 with no escape and no normalization of any form; the hash covers the decoded scalar values.
Quote and backslash escaped; solidus (/) left literal, which EX-9 requires and many JSON writers escape by default.

Stage A passes on every line including the unknown type; only its type-specific semantics go unchecked. Uses the x_ prefix EV-18 reserves, so no future registration can contradict this frozen verdict.

A registered type at an unregistered version — the half of the registry key EV-18 cannot reach, since only a registered type name can exercise it. The version is in the range EV-19 reserves, so no future contracts version may ever register it and contradict this frozen verdict. Deliberately NOT genesis: an unregistered genesis version would leave a verifier unable to extract operator_pk/registrar_pk for Stage B at all, an unresolved question that must not be frozen into a fixture.
The k=0 payload encoding: U64(0) and nothing more. No v1 type has an empty payload, so only an x_ type can pin this.

Every EX-9 branch in one string: all five short escapes (\t \n \b \f \r), \u001f in lowercase hex, escaped quote and backslash, literal solidus, literal non-ASCII. The \r is inside a string value, which EX-9 governs independently of EX-3's ban on a raw CR between lines. No v1 type may carry a control character, so an x_ type is the only way to pin the control-character branches.
The ts field is absent.
An eighth top-level field.
A field present but null. Absence is never expressed as null.
The first event does not carry seq 1.
seq jumps, leaving a gap.

An integer above 2^53-1, which no longer round-trips losslessly.
A MALFORMED type is INVALID, never PARTIAL. The PARTIAL path exists only for well-formed unregistered types; this is the boundary between them.
version below 1.
A non-object payload has no computable preimage (HA-7), so it is INVALID rather than PARTIAL: integrity cannot be confirmed even structurally.
A float in the payload. HA-7 defines no encoding for one.
A boolean in the payload.
A null payload value.

The same payload key twice: non-canonical, and never de-duplicated to conform.
Fails the syntactic gate: a space instead of T, and no milliseconds.
Passes the regex, fails the calendar gate — February 30 does not exist.
A leap second, rejected even though RFC 3339 permits it, so that a regex-only and a calendar-parsing implementation reach the same verdict.
Uppercase hex, never lowercased to conform.
The first event must anchor to 64 zeros.
Tamper matrix: prev_hash does not match the predecessor hash.
An uppercase digest.
Tamper matrix: a byte flipped in the stored hash, so the recomputed digest disagrees.
A second genesis later in the chain. genesis occurs exactly once, at seq 1.
A chain whose first line is well-formed and correctly self-signed but is not a genesis event.
Tamper matrix: an interior line dropped, breaking seq contiguity at the line that took its place.
Tamper matrix: two interior lines swapped.

EV-16's distinctive clause, which 023-028 do not reach: a payload-shape failure is INVALID *regardless of whether the (type, version) is registered*. Every other vector in this group sits on a registered type, so plain Stage A already condemns it. Here the type is unregistered, which is the case where an implementation might reach for PARTIAL instead — and must not, because HA-7 gives a float no encoding, so there is no computable preimage and EV-8's premise (integrity confirmed, semantics unchecked) fails. The stored hash is the digest of the pre-mutation event, so this line is HA-14-mismatched as well; that is unavoidable — a float has no preimage, so no hash over this line exists to store. Both failures are on line 2, so the verdict and the line are unaffected, but the vector does not isolate EV-16 from HA-14.
